title: DynProp maintenance of directed reachability
formal: Can all-pairs directed reachability be maintained from the empty graph under individual edge insertions and deletions by a fixed finite program of quantifier-free updates to auxiliary relations of arbitrary fixed finite arity, allowing arbitrary initial auxiliary relations?
definitions:
For each n≥1 the fixed universe is [n]. The input is a directed edge relation E, initially empty; loops are allowed. Inserting an existing edge or deleting an absent edge is a no-op on E. The desired binary output R contains (x,y) exactly when a directed path of length zero or more goes from x to y.

A program chooses finitely many auxiliary relation symbols, including R, each of a fixed arity independent of n. For each symbol S and each update kind it supplies a quantifier-free first-order formula phi_S(u,v,x1,…,xr) over the old input and auxiliary relations and equality. After updating edge (u,v), all auxiliary relations are replaced simultaneously by the tuples satisfying their corresponding old-state formulas. No function symbols, auxiliary functions, quantified variables or access to later updates are allowed. The formulas and arities are uniform across n and update histories.

An initial auxiliary structure may be chosen arbitrarily for each n, independently of the future update sequence. No computability restriction is imposed on this initialization. It can encode a linear order and arithmetic as static relations if desired, but not as function symbols. R is initially the diagonal. Correctness is required after every prefix of every finite update sequence. This explicitly selects all-pairs output and the strong arbitrary-initialization convention; it is not a claim about only unary or binary auxiliary storage.
answer_criterion: Give a complete Lean-checked fixed dynamic program and initialization with correctness for all n and all update sequences, or prove none exists even with the allowed initialization. Lower bounds at a fixed small auxiliary arity do not exclude all finite arities.
context:
Schwentick’s talk isolates quantifier-free maintenance of reachability as a central open question and separates relational auxiliary storage from the stronger model with functions.

Arbitrary initialization is an established convention in quantifier-free dynamic lower-bound work. It is explicitly included here.
why: This tests the expressive power of quantifier-free dynamic computation beyond known bounded-arity lower bounds.

import_provenance.original_title: Can quantifier-free updates maintain directed reachability?
import_provenance.original_statement: Is directed reachability maintainable under single-edge insertions and deletions by quantifier-free update formulas with a fixed finite collection of auxiliary relations of arbitrary fixed arity (DynProp)? Schwentick’s question is about unrestricted relational auxiliary arity, beyond known lower bounds for bounded-arity subclasses.
import_provenance.supplied_caveat: Remark: First-order updates with quantifiers already maintain directed reachability (2015); that result does not settle DynProp.

sentences: Edges change one at a time on a fixed finite vertex set.
Auxiliary relations must always contain the exact all-pairs reachability answer.
Each replacement tuple is determined by a quantifier-free formula on the previous state.
The program may use any fixed finite auxiliary arity and arbitrary initial relational data.
Auxiliary functions and bulk changes are outside the selected model.
